## Professional Summary
Postdoctoral researcher with strong foundations in multi-variable calculus, linear algebra, and stochastic processes. Expert in solving complex multi-variable systems and formulating analytical solutions for high-dimensional geometric problems and implementing numerical validations using Mathematica and Python. Proven track record of high-level mathematical problem solving, evidenced by top-tier national rankings (Top 10 in India) and fellowships at Caltech/LIGO.

## Education
* **PhD, Department of Theoretical Physics**, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), Mumbai, India (2019-2024).
  * Thesis Advisor: Prof. Abhijit Gadde.
  * Thesis Title: "Multi-partite entanglement in holography".
  * Focus: Thermodynamic instabilities of Black Holes in Holography, Decoherence in Open Quantum Systems.
* **Integrated BS-MS - Dual degree in Physics and Mathematics**, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India (2014-2019).
  * CGPA: 8.83/10.
  * Master's Thesis Advisor: Prof. Bindusar Sahoo.
  * Master's Thesis Title: "Kaluza-Klein reductions and AdS/RF correspondence".

## Professional Experience
* **Postdoctoral Researcher**, Leinweber Center for Theoretical Physics (University of Michigan) (2024 - Present). Investigating thermodynamic phases of supersymmetric systems in a multidimensional parameter space using quantitative analysis in Mathematica and Python.
* **Doctoral Researcher**, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) (2019-2024). Developed novel mathematical measures for quantifying multi-party entanglement in quantum systems, and established monotonicity properties for such measures. Designed and implemented a semidefinite programming algorithm in Mathematica to optimize separability detection in high-dimensional quantum states. Formulated analytical solutions for holographic duals of information theoretic measures, reducing complex high-dimensional geometry problems into tractable group theoretic computations.
* **Summer Research Fellow**, LIGO Laboratory, California Institute of Technology (Caltech) (May 2017 - July 2017). Characterized Brownian noise in candidate coatings on the silicon mirrors used in the Interferometers. Designed and Implemented an All Digital Phase Locked Loop in a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to study the Brownian noise from the experimental setup. Devised several compression techniques to improve the efficiency of the digital circuit.
* **Hardware-Software Integration**, Everyday Radio Telescope | IISER-TVM (2016). Constructed a radio telescope from everyday objects with fellow astronomy enthusiasts. Performed signal acquisition and processed astronomical data using Python/C++ for spectral analysis.
